## Definition check

The section headed “Source rubric and schema paths (#158)” is present in my instructions. The sentence beginning “Read release-specific notes” reads, verbatim and in full:

> Read release-specific notes from the dedicated `updates.update_details` field, `updates.description` or `notes`, requiring actual release or derivation information rather than crediting unrelated notes.

That matches the current rules (dedicated-field mapping for release notes, alongside the `at_risk_populations`, `data_governance.committee_contact` and Element 8 processing-role mappings in the same section), so I proceeded.

## Validation

```
poetry run python scripts/validate_evaluation_schema.py --file output_evaluation.json --rubric rubric10-semantic
VALID output_evaluation.json: rubric10-semantic
```
Exit status 0. (The sandbox refused a `cd`-compound invocation; I ran the identical command from the working directory instead.)

## Result: 49/50

| Element | Score |
|---|---|
| 1 Discovery and Identification | 5/5 |
| 2 Access and Retrieval | 5/5 |
| 3 Reuse and Interoperability | 5/5 |
| 4 Ethical Use and Privacy | 5/5 |
| 5 Composition and Structure | 5/5 |
| 6 Provenance and Versioning | 5/5 |
| 7 Motivation and Funding | 5/5 |
| 8 Technical Transparency | **4/5** |
| 9 Limitations Disclosure | 5/5 |
| 10 Cross-Platform Integration | 5/5 |

`total_points` 49, `max_points` 50, `excluded_max_points` 0, `adjusted_max_points` 50 — so `normalized_percentage` and `fixed_percentage` are both 98.0 over the same denominator, and `sub_elements_not_applicable` is 0.

**Applicability.** All five trigger conditions resolved as satisfied on evidence external to the gated elements, so nothing was excluded: human subjects from the E1 description and E8 collection mechanisms; the governance constraint from E2 (`confidentiality_level: restricted`, applying NIH GDS obligations); datasets-shared from `distribution_formats`, the FAIRhub pages and a download-granting licence; software-output from the `github.com/AI-READI` repository reference; collection-identified from `acquisition_methods` and `collection_mechanisms`. Each conditional sub-element carries `applicability_status` and `applicability_evidence`.

**The single 0** is Element 8 sub-element 4. It is applicable — the release was demonstrably processed, and per #1079/#1081 the item is not gated on whether a repository is pointed at. It scores 0 because no software is named in a producing or transforming role: the `.fda`/`.sdt`→DICOM, `.FIT`→Open mHealth and `.xml`→WFDB conversions are all described in the passive voice, and every named tool sits in an excluded role — REDCap and MoCA Duo in capture (a), FAIRhub and Azure in hosting (b), the OMOP Data Quality Dashboard in validation (d) — with the GitHub link an organisation account root that identifies only the publisher.

**Consistency:** 22 passed, 2 failed, 7 warnings. The notable pass is arithmetic: per-directory file counts plus 9 root metadata files sum to exactly 356,343, and three cohort breakdowns plus the splits each total 2,280. The notable failure is the deidentification contradiction — `is_deidentified.method` says “NoDeIdentification / no identifiers were collected” while `participant_privacy` describes HIPAA Safe Harbor removal of PHI and `identifiers_removed` enumerates what was removed. The item still passes on a detailed, actionable method description, with the contradiction recorded as medium severity.

Model recorded as `claude-opus-5[1m]` for both `name` and `evaluator_model`; `temperature: null` with the note that this runtime does not expose it.
